title: Blum speedup theorem for arbitrary complexity measures
statement: For a Blum complexity measure and a computable speedup factor, there is a computable function such that every program computing it has another program computing it that meets the prescribed cost improvement on all but finitely many inputs; the exact hypotheses on the factor must be confirmed from source.

source.citation: M. Blum, A machine-independent theory of the complexity of recursive functions, JACM 14 (1967); Aristotle completion email received 2026-08-11

criteria: complete Aristotle source bundle imported into the pinned repository toolchain
lake build succeeds with no sorry, admit, native_decide, or added axioms
#print axioms is contained in propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound
inspect the exact hypotheses on the speedup factor, the Blum measure axioms, halting/cost-domain equivalence, cofinite quantifier, recursion-theorem construction, and no-fastest-algorithm corollary

notes: Aristotle reports a theorem uniform over Blum measures and computable speedup factors. No public Lean proof was located in the limited search. Semantic novelty depends on the exact type and growth assumptions for the factor r; the source must show that the claimed theorem really yields 'no fastest algorithm.'
